findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.ts:172-206 (CHK-001b) — the delegation-equivalence check leaks the REAL invoking process cwd/git-branch into the fixture comparison via the pre-existing detectDoneStoryWorktreeContext(invocationCwd = process.cwd()) default (packages/main/src/handlers/done-effects.ts:625), which runStoryTransition calls unconditionally for phase=DONE. Reproduced: running `node dist/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.js` from inside the B-d877 worktree makes both errA/errB collide on the leaked real branch text ("refusing DONE cleanup: detected branch story/B-d877 but expected story/SID"), i.e. the assertion passes only because both calls incidentally observe the SAME wrong ambient branch — not because dev_merge genuinely delegates to the same DONE business-gate logic. Running the identical unmodified build from /tmp (outside any git worktree) produces a completely different, deterministic pair ("Cannot enter DONE: no test evidence (run lattice validate first)") that DOES exercise the real DONE gate. So the check's pass is environment-dependent/coincidental rather than a rigorous proof of delegation; it could in principle diverge (false pass or false fail) depending on unrelated ambient git state at invocation time. Separately, checklist verificationEvidence notes "transition-integrity smoke (17 checks)" but the committed file (unchanged since headHash 30499ca7e1) actually emits 19 [✓] lines end-to-end — the recorded check count in the evidence note does not match the delivered smoke.

concept-cleanup: dev_finish's target phase changed from TEST to REVIEW (raw-actor+PHASE_TO_EVENT mislabel removed, now runStoryTransition CODE_REVIEW->REVIEW), but the sibling dev_merge guard in packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts (phase-check just before the CHK-001 runStoryTransition(DONE) call, ~line 1092) still throws `Story ${args.storyId} is currently in phase ${story.phase}; you need to dev_finish first to enter TEST` when phase is not TEST/DONE. This is the old raw-actor-era assumption that dev_finish lands the story directly in TEST; it was scrubbed from dev_finish's own event push but left verbatim in dev_merge's error text within the SAME two functions this story retargets. Post-diff, calling dev_finish only reaches REVIEW; a caller in DEV or REVIEW hitting dev_merge is told a factually wrong next step (dev_finish does not put the story into TEST). Confirmed both the old text and the actual current runtime behavior via: `grep -n "first to enter TEST" packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts` and the transition-integrity-smoke.js run showing dev_finish lands in REVIEW.

quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/story-transition-lock.ts:54-55,93-94 (staleMs=120000/deadlineMs=180000) + packages/main/src/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.ts:210-260 (CHK-002a) — the per-story transition lock is a plain mtime-based mkdir lock with NO heartbeat/liveness renewal, so a holder that is scheduled off-CPU for >120s while still alive (not crashed) can have its lock force-reclaimed by a waiting same-owner transition, producing exactly the double-mint this story exists to prevent. This is not hypothetical: re-running the delivered, unmodified `node dist/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.js` repeatedly on this review host, CHK-002a failed once out of ~15 runs with `successes===1` false — both concurrent workers reported {ok:true,phase:REVIEW} (a genuine double-mint), correlating with host load average ~36 on a 10-core machine at the time; 0/14 other runs failed as load dropped to ~15-25. staleMs=120000 matches the already-accepted sibling convention (MAIN_WRITE_LOCK_STALE_MS / VALIDATION_EXECUTION_LOCK_STALE_MS are also 120000), so this is not a novel regression introduced by this diff's specific choice of threshold, and is very unlikely under normal (non-contended) operation since a fixture-scale REVIEW transition with no worktree/git calls should complete in milliseconds. Flagging because the reviewer task explicitly asks to confirm the lock's stale/deadline choices are sane and because it is directly reproducible evidence against the story's core "exactly one succeeds" claim under host contention; recommend the story or a follow-up note that this smoke can flake on a heavily loaded shared CI/dev host for reasons unrelated to a code regression (mkdir-lock family has no heartbeat renewal to distinguish slow-but-alive from crashed), rather than being silently re-run until green.

concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/handlers/hints.ts:176-178 devFinishHint (registered for the dev_finish command at hints.ts:254, fired unconditionally by cli-engine.ts decorateResult on every plain-text `dev_finish` CLI call) still carries the pre-B-d877 raw-actor-era assumption that dev_finish is the terminal/merge step: it returns literally `\u2192 Worktree \u5df2\u5408\u5e76\u56de\u672c\u5730 main\u3002\u53ef\u4ee5\u5f00\u59cb\u4e0b\u4e00\u4e2a story\uff1b...` ("Worktree has been merged back to local main. You can start the next story..."). Post-fix, dev_finish (worktree.ts:1000) only advances DEV\u2192REVIEW via runStoryTransition and its OWN result text says `Worktree preserved: ${wtPath}` + `Run code review in the worktree; after review passes, advance to TEST` \u2014 nothing is merged and the worktree is explicitly kept. So a live `dev_finish` invocation now prints a directly self-contradictory two-line combo (\"Worktree preserved...\" immediately followed by the hint \"Worktree already merged back to main, start the next story\"), and an operator following the hint would skip the mandatory REVIEW step this exact story exists to enforce. There is no corresponding hint registered for `dev_merge` (the function that ACTUALLY performs the git merge) \u2014 grep -n dev_merge packages/main/src/handlers/hints.ts returns nothing \u2014 strongly suggesting this hint text was originally meant for dev_merge and was mis-keyed under dev_finish. This is the same conceptual family already identified and fixed in the sibling dev_merge precondition message by round-1 finding F-002 (dev_finish assumed to land in / complete TEST), but was missed here. Not exercised by transition-integrity-smoke.ts, which calls handlers.dev_finish(...) directly and bypasses the CLI decorateResult/hint layer entirely.

adversarial-repro: packages/main/src/core/story-transition-lock.ts:94-114 (classifyTransitionLockHolder) — the round-2 liveness classifier checks only whether SOME process currently exists with the recorded pid on the recorded host (process.kill(pid,0)); it never verifies that live process is actually the SAME process instance that originally acquired the lock (e.g. via a recorded process-start-time). Confirmed by direct repro: calling the compiled classifyTransitionLockHolder with a snapshot whose holder.pid is set to an unrelated but genuinely live pid on this host (this shell's ppid) and ageMs=10 minutes (>> staleMs=120000) returns classification="active" — i.e. a lock whose true original holder crashed minutes ago is permanently un-reclaimable as long as its old pid happens to have been recycled by any other live process, which is common on any long-uptime/busy host given the OS pid namespace is finite and this very smoke test alone spawns ~50 short-lived child pids per 25 runs. Effect: every subsequent story_advance for that story blocks for the full acquire deadline (STORY_TRANSITION_DEADLINE_MS=180000ms in the same file) and then hard-fails with an opaque lock-timeout error, requiring manual deletion of the stale .lattice/locks/transition/<id>.lock dir to recover — a self-inflicted, non-obvious denial-of-service, not a data-corrupting double-mint, but still a real regression in availability versus the pre-fix mtime-only behavior (which at least reclaimed after staleMs regardless of pid games). The codebase already has an established, stronger pattern for this exact hazard in the sibling lock family: packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts:85-126 (classifyValidationExecutionLock) cross-checks a heartbeat file's freshness AND processStartTimeMs (via sameProcessStart) before trusting a live pid, specifically to rule out pid-reuse impersonating the real holder. story-transition-lock.ts' MkdirLockHolderInfo already carries an optional processStartTimeMs field (mkdir-lock.ts:49) but acquireStoryTransitionLock's holderInfo (story-transition-lock.ts:151-156) never populates it, and classifyTransitionLockHolder never consults it — so the sibling's defense was not carried over to this new classifier.

quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:270-285 (release()) — the ownership-checked release only protects callers that pass holderInfo (main-write-lock.ts:205, validation-execution-lock.ts:249, story-transition-lock.ts:158). The scope-contract for this fix round explicitly records the change as "back-compatible for all other callers" (.lattice/story/actives/B-d877/scope-contract.json:20), which means every OTHER real, shipped caller of the SAME shared primitive still takes the old unconditional-rm branch at mkdir-lock.ts:273-276 (releaseLockId stays undefined because no holderInfo is ever passed) and therefore remains exposed to the identical delete-successor race this round exists to close: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:100-102 (withChecklistLock, checklist.lock), packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:82-84 (withReviewPassLock, review-passes.lock), packages/main/src/handlers/review-run.ts:26-28 (withReviewRunLock, review-runs.lock), and packages/main/src/handlers/init-check.ts:64-66 (withInitCheckLock, init-check.lock) all call withMkdirLock with only a {label} option — no holderInfo, no classifyExistingLock — so they use the DEFAULT staleMs=10000ms/mtime-only reclaim (mkdir-lock.ts:164) with NO liveness check at all. Concretely: if holder A (e.g. a checklist_update call) is legitimately slow past 10s under host load (this review reproduced host load average 36-57 causing multi-second scheduling delays on this very machine while probing CHK-002a), a waiting caller B will mtime-stale-reclaim A's checklist.lock dir and acquire it; when A eventually finishes and calls release(), release() unconditionally rmSyncs the dir — deleting B's still-active lock out from under it, opening the door to a third caller C acquiring concurrently with B and both writing checklist.json/review-passes.json/etc. at once (lost-update / corrupted metadata), i.e. the exact bug class the commit message attributes to "codex HIGH" and claims to close at the primitive level, but which this diff only closes for the 3 opted-in callers, not these 4 real production ones.

All 6 must-priority verificationIntent items (CHK-001:happy/edge/adversarial:0, CHK-002:happy/edge/adversarial:0) have STALE verificationEvidence that does not correspond to the round-2 fix commit 9cb145baf6 (mkdir-lock ownership-checked release, story-transition-lock pid-liveness classifier, uniform DONE transition-lock ordering, +CHK-002c/002d, smoke grown 17->29 checks). checklist.json still records headHash=30499ca7e1ae5632205216797c29faeb50de045f / materialHash=b54d07bfd0224d6542d575a9daf4416d8bf4113636cb0118554c6a47c96c3cab (the pre-fix commit) with note text unchanged since round 1 ("transition-integrity smoke (17 checks)") even though the delivered packages/main/src/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.ts now runs 29 checks. Confirmed two independent ways: (1) `lattice evidence_inspect --storyId=B-d877 --format=json` returns freshness.status=stale, staleRefs=7 (all 6 checklist refs + test-evidence), currentMaterialHash=340d4635ab4fb2ff7b7a4682b0c316bd0bdb23bd1ca724866bdb33c5109d4656 (differs from recorded); (2) `lattice validate --story=B-d877 --json` independently returns status=fail, summary="Project validation commands failed; verification coverage missing 6 required intent(s)", and refuses routine-validation reuse with refusalReasons=[material-hash-changed-or-missing, story-files-hash-changed-or-missing, untrusted-lineage-path:packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts, untrusted-lineage-path:packages/main/src/core/story-transition-lock.ts, untrusted-lineage-path:packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts, untrusted-lineage-path:packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts, untrusted-lineage-path:packages/main/src/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.ts]. No verification_evidence_add/batch_add command was run after fix commit 9cb145baf6 (git log shows only DEV/REVIEW/scope-ack/finding_resolve metadata commits between the fix and current HEAD). Note this is a pure evidence-recording gap, not a code-correctness defect: this reviewer independently rebuilt an isolated detached worktree at current HEAD and confirmed the unmodified smoke passes 29/29, and adversarially confirmed CHK-002c/002d are load-bearing (reverting mkdir-lock.ts release() ownership check to unconditional rmSync makes CHK-002d fail; reverting classifyTransitionLockHolder to always return unknown makes CHK-002c fail; restoring both files returns 29/29). Action: re-run `node packages/main/dist/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.js` against current HEAD and record fresh verification_evidence_add/batch_add for all 6 intents with current headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash, then re-run lattice validate to clear the coverage gap before requesting review pass.

concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts:992 (dev_start return text, fires on every dev_start CLI/handler call) still says: `→ After development completes, call dev_finish(${args.storyId}) to merge back to the main branch`. This is the SAME raw-actor-era misconception already fixed twice elsewhere in this exact file/story (round-1 F-002 fixed the dev_merge precondition message assuming dev_finish lands in TEST; round-2 F-004 fixed hints.ts devFinishHint claiming dev_finish merged to main) but was missed in this third location. Post-fix, dev_finish (worktree.ts:1000) only advances DEV->REVIEW via runStoryTransition and its own result text correctly says `Worktree preserved: ${wtPath}` + `Run code review in the worktree; after review passes, advance to TEST` -- nothing is merged, the worktree stays. The actual merge-to-main only happens later via dev_merge at TEST->DONE (worktree.ts:1056, confirmed by runStoryTransition phase=DONE -> applyDoneMergeEffects). So a user who just ran dev_start sees this text as the very next instruction, is told the wrong function name performs the wrong action, and would expect a merge that will not happen for at least one more phase transition (REVIEW->TEST) after calling dev_finish. Confirmed pre-existing (unchanged by this diff: `git show main:packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts` has byte-identical text at line 989) and confirmed no other reference to this phrase remains anywhere else in the repo (`grep -rn "merge back to the main branch"` across *.ts/*.md returns only this one line).

adversarial-repro (F-005 residual): packages/main/src/core/story-transition-lock.ts:146-153 (classifyTransitionLockHolder) — the round-3 PID-reuse guard only fires when `holder.pid === process.pid` (line 150), i.e. it can only detect that ITS OWN reclaiming process happens to have inherited the recorded pid. For the general/realistic case reported in the original F-005 (a DIFFERENT, unrelated, genuinely-live process on the host has since been assigned the crashed holder's recycled pid), the classifier still returns 'active' forever regardless of age, exactly like pre-fix. Reproduced directly: `classifyTransitionLockHolder({holder:{pid:<a live pid that is NOT process.pid, e.g. process.ppid>, hostname: os.hostname(), processStartTimeMs: Date.now()-99*3600000, lockId:'orig'}, ageMs: 600000, staleMs:120000, ...})` returns `'active'` even though ageMs (10min) >> staleMs and the recorded processStartTimeMs is wildly wrong — because the pid!==process.pid branch never runs the mismatch check. This means a crashed transition-lock holder whose pid gets recycled by ANY other live process (not just a coincidental self-respawn) is still permanently un-reclaimable, reproducing the same story_advance DoS the original F-005 described. The round-3 fix's own smoke check (CHK-002c in transition-integrity-smoke.ts) only exercises the narrow self-pid case (`pid: process.pid`), so it never catches this. The claimed parity with packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts (classifyValidationExecutionLock) is also inaccurate: that sibling's REAL defense against foreign pid-reuse is a HEARTBEAT freshness check (heartbeatAgeMs/heartbeatLooksMismatched, validation-execution-lock.ts:88-100), which classifyTransitionLockHolder never ported over (no heartbeat file is ever written by acquireStoryTransitionLock) — only the narrow self-pid start-time comparison was mirrored, not the mechanism that actually generalizes to foreign pids.

adversarial-repro (CAS fence is not atomic): packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:725-746 — the round-3 "CAS-at-persist correctness fence" (re-read story via store.readStory, compare persistedBeforeWrite.phase to oldPhase, then store.writeStory) is a plain read-then-write, NOT an atomic compare-and-swap: store.ts readStory/writeStory (packages/main/src/core/store.ts:174-182) are independent readFileSync/writeFileSync calls with no OS-level lock, no O_EXCL, and no version/CAS primitive tying the read to the write. The code comment explicitly claims "this CAS is the AUTHORITATIVE correctness guarantee and does not depend on the lock having held" (transition-orchestrator.ts:733-734) — this claim is false for genuine cross-process concurrency. Reproduced directly: wrote a standalone 2-process repro that mirrors the exact pattern (readStory(oldPhase check) -> [scheduling gap] -> writeStory) against the REAL StoryStore class with NO lock at all; when both processes' re-reads land before either writeStory (simulating what happens if the transition lock's exclusivity is ever defeated, e.g. by the still-open PID-reuse gap in the sibling finding B-d877:F-009), BOTH racers observe phase===oldPhase, BOTH pass the "CAS" check, and BOTH call writeStory -> a genuine double-mint (two distinct currentReviewRound values written, the second silently clobbering the first, exactly the bug class CHK-002 exists to prevent). Full repro script + output available on request. The existing smoke coverage for this (CHK-002c4 in transition-integrity-smoke.ts) does NOT test this: it runs entirely SINGLE-PROCESS, using a Proxy to inject a synthetic already-changed read result at one specific read index within one JS call stack — this can only model a strictly-SEQUENTIAL race (a second transition whose read happens after the first transition's write already committed), which a plain re-read-and-compare genuinely does catch. It never models two truly concurrent OS processes racing the CAS window itself, so it cannot support the "does not depend on the lock having held" claim, and my repro shows that claim does not hold. Recommend either (a) softening the code comment to state this fence only defends against sequential/late-starting transitions, not true concurrent races, and continuing to rely on the transition lock as the actual exclusion mechanism (in which case F-009 should be fully closed first), or (b) making the persist step genuinely atomic (e.g. an OS-level file lock spanning read+write, or a version-checked atomic rename).

lattice validate does NOT currently pass, contradicting this round's premise. validate.commands[33] (node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js), part of the SAME validate suite that produced the fresh headHash=32c692758861/materialHash=0a0ab8fe07... evidence recorded for all 6 CHK-001/CHK-002 must-priority intents, fails deterministically with `quorum_submit refuses: worktree/index must be clean before the atomic verdict batch; pre-existing bytes were left untouched: D .lattice/story/actives/B-quorum-smoke/review-passes.lock/holder.json` at the check `worktree-local CLI commits the exact quorum batch through the production entrypoint` (quorum-submit-smoke.ts:690). Root cause: this story's R2 fix (mkdir-lock.ts, universal ownership-checked release, commit da8445c461) made EVERY acquireMkdirLock call ALWAYS write a holder.json token inside the lock dir, including the checklist/finding/review-run/init-check lock family that lives INSIDE the committed story directory (previously an invisible empty mkdir/rmdir with no file). quorum-submit-smoke.ts's own synthetic fixture .gitignore (line 138: only .lattice/autopilot-verdicts/, .lattice/activity.jsonl, .lattice/locks/) does not exclude these in-story-dir *.lock/ dirs the way this dev repo's ROOT .gitignore was ad-hoc patched to (commits 32c692758861/87b66fa49a, applied only to THIS worktree, not shipped as a durable code fix or propagated to the test fixture). recordReviewerPasses() commits the story tree while a review-passes.lock/holder.json is transiently present, then a later release() rmSyncs it, leaving a D (deleted) diff that trips the strict clean-worktree check quorum_submit itself enforces. Reproduced deterministically 3/3 in the story worktree AND 1/1 in a from-scratch `git worktree add --detach` isolated copy with an independent `npm run build` (ruling out shared-worktree/other-lane contamination): `node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js` fails identically both times with git status clean immediately before each run. This matches codex round-3 cross-host finding #4 (already surfaced in this round's adversarial transcript) but is not yet tracked as a lattice finding_add; recording independently since it directly bears on evidence trustworthiness for verification-coverage: the recorded per-intent "pass" evidence for CHK-001/CHK-002 comes from a code state whose OVERALL `lattice validate` run fails, so this story cannot legitimately be considered validate-clean or proceed toward TEST/DONE on the current HEAD. Fix: relocate checklist/finding/review-run/init-check lock dirs to the shared `.lattice/locks/` runtime root (matching how this same round already fixed the story-transition-lock's own git-tracked-story-dir hazard via resolveSharedLockRoot), or make holder.json writes conditional/excluded from every git/scope/material consumer including test fixtures.

adversarial-repro: packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:703-714 (IDEA->PLAN store.writeChecklist(args.checklist)) sits BEFORE the R4 atomic persist claim (:750-788) and is NOT protected by it. The claim (and its docstring in story-transition-lock.ts:24-40, e.g. "ANY mis-classification or stale-reclaim of THIS [advisory] lock ... can ONLY cause redundant gate work -- NEVER a double-mint") only guards story.phase / currentReviewRound / the phase_transition event; writeChecklist runs unconditionally on args.checklist for BOTH racers before either reaches the claim, so under an advisory-lock bypass (LATTICE_TEST_DISABLE_TRANSITION_ADVISORY_LOCK=1, or a genuine defeat of the advisory lock such as the residual PID-reuse gap previously tracked as F-009/F-005) the checklist.json actually persisted on disk is simply whichever process's writeChecklist ran last -- INDEPENDENT of which process wins the atomic claim and actually persists phase=PLAN. Reproduced with two real concurrent OS processes racing runStoryTransition with phase set to PLAN for the same fixture story with DIFFERENT checklist payloads (advisory lock bypassed): in 10/15 rounds the checklist.json content on disk came from the LOSING transition (the one whose phase-write the atomic claim correctly rejected with the error text concurrent transition already advanc...), while story.phase correctly reflected only the winner. So a caller who legitimately wins the phase-mint race can end up with a PERSISTED CHECKLIST THAT IS NOT THE ONE IT SUBMITTED, silently, with no error surfaced -- a real state-corruption sibling to the double-mint bug this story closes, just outside the claim's protected span. Contrast with the DONE path: its analogous pre-claim side effect (captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore at :692) IS safe because acquireDoneMainMergeLock (:544) is a REAL (non-advisory) mkdir lock acquired well before actor.send/closeoutCapture, so a second concurrent DONE attempt cannot reach that code at all; PLAN has no equivalent real lock -- only the advisory transitionLock, which this same round explicitly documents as best-effort/non-authoritative. Recommend either widening the atomic claim to cover the writeChecklist branch too (re-read+compare oldPhase before writing checklist, same pattern as the phase persist), or moving the writeChecklist call to occur only after the claim confirms this transition is the actual winner.

packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:755-767 — the R3 FIX A doc comment self-contradicts: line 755 says the atomic persist claim (mkdir claim at persistClaimPath) "is what makes a double-mint impossible" (unqualified/absolute), then the immediately-following KNOWN LIMITATION (lines 757-767) documents that the SAME claim is "NOT an absolute mutex" and that "a waiter could then stale-reclaim a still-live holders claim" under an OS-freeze scenario — i.e. the double-mint the first sentence calls impossible is exactly what the second paragraph says can still occur in that residual case. Contrast with core/story-transition-lock.ts, which scopes its own never-a-double-mint claim correctly to the ADVISORY lock only (not to the persist claim itself), so it does not have this problem. A reader who stops at line 755 (or greps for "impossible") gets a materially wrong correctness guarantee for the exact mechanism the KNOWN-LIMITATION note exists to caveat. Fix: soften line 755 to something like "makes a double-mint impossible under the normal software-concurrency threat model (see KNOWN LIMITATION below for the OS-freeze residual)" so the two paragraphs agree.

packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:336-348 (release(), fail-open branch reachable by every withMkdirLock caller that omits requireHolderToken, e.g. process-events.ts/checklist.ts/finding.ts/init-check.ts/review-run.ts/agent-prompt.ts): when releaseLockId===undefined (our own original holder.json write failed at acquire), release() treats `readMkdirLockHolder(lockDir)===null` as proof no successor is present and calls removeEmptyLockDirNonRecursive -> rmdirSync(lockDir). But readMkdirLockHolder also returns null when a successor B has just won mkdirSync(lockDir) (the atomic race) and has NOT YET reached its own writeFileSync(holder.json) a few lines later inside acquireMkdirLock -- B's dir is genuinely empty at that instant, so the non-recursive rmdirSync SUCCEEDS and deletes B's freshly-created lock dir out from under it. B then continues (its writeFileSync throws ENOENT into a missing dir; without requireHolderToken it falls into the same fail-open PROBE catch and returns as if it still holds the lock), so a THIRD process can now mkdirSync the same path and BOTH B and the third process believe they hold the mutex. This is a real improvement over the pre-fix unconditional rmSync (which deleted 100% of the time), and it requires the precondition that OUR OWN original write already failed, so it is a narrow, compound-rare race -- but it is a new angle not covered by the CHK-002d test (which only exercises the ownership-checked releaseLockId!==undefined branch) or by the documented OS-freeze/staleMs known-limitation (this trigger is a write failure, not a time-based stale reclaim). Recommend a follow-up: in the null-holder case, treat `existsSync(lockDir) && readdirSync(lockDir).length>0` differently, or simply never remove non-recursively without re-checking mtime age (dir just created by us vs by a fresh successor).

packages/main/src/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.ts:253 (APPEND_HELPERS = new Set(["appendRawProcessEventBytes","appendProcessEventRecord"])) omits the third exported free function from core/process-events.ts, `appendProcessEvent` (process-events.ts:64-70, also exported with a now-mandatory lockDir param). The CHK-002c8 AST regression guard (appendHelperMissingRelocatedLock, same file :263-293) only walks CallExpressions whose callee identifier is in APPEND_HELPERS, so a future production file that imports and calls the bare `appendProcessEvent` directly (not via StoryStore.appendProcessEvent, which already threads runtimeLockDirPath correctly) would NOT be flagged by CHK-002c8 even if it passes a hardcoded/non-relocated lockDir string -- the guard's own referencesRelocatedResolver check would never run for that call site. TypeScript's now-mandatory 3rd parameter still prevents an outright missing argument, but not a wrong-but-present one, which is exactly the class of regression CHK-002c8 ("codex #3 regression guard") and the commit message ("process-events lockDir is now MANDATORY so no writer regresses") claim is covered. No current call site is affected (grepped: only process-events.ts internal forwarding and store.ts's aliased-import call site exist today), so this is not a live bug, but it is a real completeness gap in a guard whose stated purpose is exhaustive writer coverage. Fix: add 'appendProcessEvent' to APPEND_HELPERS.

packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:328-361 (release(), B-d877 R4 codex-#2 fix) leaks the lock directory on EVERY clean release for any caller that stores auxiliary files inside lockDir alongside holder.json. release() now does rmSync(join(lockDir, holder.json)) then removeEmptyLockDirNonRecursive(lockDir) i.e. a non-recursive rmdirSync that silently no-ops on ENOTEMPTY. packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts writeValidationHeartbeat() writes heartbeat.json into that SAME lockDir (VALIDATION_EXECUTION_LOCK_HEARTBEAT_FILE, used by withValidationExecutionLock, the wrapper around every lattice validate --story=X call in handlers/verifier.ts:1206/1284 and handlers/done-required-validation.ts). After a clean release, holder.json is removed but heartbeat.json remains, so rmdirSync fails ENOTEMPTY and the dir leaks (now holder-less) until VALIDATION_EXECUTION_LOCK_STALE_MS=120000ms elapses, blocking every subsequent validate/done_required_validate call on that story with a false already-running refusal. Verified deterministically (100% repro, not load-related): patched a throwaway dist copy of validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts with a debug probe and confirmed the testCase=command scenario leaves .lattice/locks/validation/<story>.lock containing ONLY heartbeat.json after the first done_required_validate call completes cleanly, then the immediate retry fails with refusalReasons=[already running...by another Proofbound process (holder details unavailable), heartbeat 1s ago...]. This is a real regression from this round: prior to 580d28eee0 release() used rmSync(lockDir,{recursive:true,force:true}) which always fully removed heartbeat.json too. Consequence: running node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.js (validate.commands[9] of the 46 configured lattice.config.json validate commands) FAILS deterministically (10/10 reproductions) with command timeout must permit a successful immediate rerun / 1 !== 0, so lattice validate --story=B-d877 does not genuinely pass end-to-end.
